# libiio-utils

**Command-line tools that find and talk to IIO devices such as the PlutoSDR and ADALM2000**

- **Version recorded:** 0.26
- **Categories:** `electronics`, `sdr-hardware`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/analogdevicesinc/libiio>

## What it does

The command-line tools of libiio, Analog Devices' library for Industrial I/O devices. `iio_info` lists the contexts it can reach and every device, channel and attribute inside one; `iio_attr` reads and writes a single attribute (a Pluto's LO frequency, gain or sample rate); `iio_readdev` and `iio_writedev` stream raw samples to and from a file or a pipe; `iio_reg` reads and writes device registers.

## Why you would want it

The PlutoSDR and the ADALM2000 are IIO devices, reached over USB or the network through libiio rather than through a /dev node. When SDR software does not see a Pluto, `iio_info -S` answers the first question -- does libiio see it at all, and at which URI -- before any application is involved. It is the Pluto's equivalent of `rtl_test` and `hackrf_info`.

## Before it will work

An IIO device, attached over USB or reachable on the network (a Pluto answers at `ip:192.168.2.1` over its USB network interface by default, per Analog Devices' documentation; not checked here). USB access needs a udev rule, which the plutosdr hardware entry does not yet carry: its identifier is unconfirmed.

## Install and launch

- **Installed with the profile:** [`electronics`](../profiles/electronics.md).
- **Install:** `hammunition install libiio-utils --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Commands it leaves on your PATH: `iio_scan`.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `libiio-utils`

## Known problems

Unmeasured with hardware here: the maintainer owns no PlutoSDR and no ADALM2000, so no scan has been run against a device. The archives carry the 0.x tools while upstream has tagged v1.0.0; whether a command written for 1.x runs unchanged on the packaged 0.x tools is unmeasured, so check `iio_info --help` when an example fails. Ubuntu 24.04 and Mint 22.3 carry 0.25, the others 0.26 (measured 2026-09-30).

## Keeping it current

- probe: apt policy
- strategy: apt_upgrade
- Upstream is active and has moved to a 1.x series with a changed API; the archives carry 0.25 and 0.26. A 1.x tools package would arrive through the distribution.
